title: Local Geometry of Least Squares for Unmixing Signals with Parameter-Dependent Dictionaries
summary: Modeling signals as linear combinations of atoms from a dictionary is ubiquitous in modern signal processing. In the finite-dimensional setting, whenever atoms depend nonlinearly upon unknown parameters, the signal model is said to be separable. In this work, we study least-squares reconstruction of separable signals and establish a unified theoretical framework for their analysis. We introduce the unmixing metric, a distance that captures the distinct roles and sensitivities of linear and nonlinear parameters, and establish local convergence and stability guarantees under its topology.
